tool_args.content: Post-STEMI medication reconciliation based on discharge context: patient is 4 days post-discharge after STEMI treated with emergency PCI and imported drug-eluting stent. Discharge regimen is aspirin plus ticagrelor for 12 months and indefinite statin therapy for secondary prevention. Follow-up cardiovascular exam notes stable hemodynamics and no recurrent chest pain at discharge. Authorized follow-up CBC and renal function remain adequate for ongoing dual-antiplatelet and statin therapy. Cardiology consult recommends continuing aspirin plus ticagrelor for the full 12 months and maintaining statin therapy unless new bleeding, intolerance, or other contraindication emerges, with cardiology follow-up within 1 month. No alternative prior medication history was provided. Reconciliation assessment: regimen is internally consistent with recent STEMI/PCI discharge plan; continue current therapy and counsel not to stop antiplatelet therapy without cardiology guidance. Monitoring gap: only CBC/renal follow-up was authorized/released here; no liver panel was available in the scoped data.

tool_args.justification: Recent STEMI treated with PCI/drug-eluting stent, currently stable without recurrent chest pain, and follow-up CBC/renal function remain adequate for ongoing aspirin, ticagrelor, and statin therapy. Cardiology recommends maintaining the discharge regimen with cardiology follow-up within one month. Escalate sooner for chest pain, dyspnea, syncope, major bleeding, melena, or medication intolerance.
